title: access: changing an object's sharing model to public_read_write after it was first published leaves members unable to edit records they can read — the #8023 write-floor exemption does not follow the change (detail withheld pending maintainer)
body:
Filing gate: ① product defect, reproduced twice, landing site named (maintainer direct dispatch, authorizing words quoted in the audit comment).

## Symptom (customer-visible)

An admin changes an existing object's org-wide default to **Public read/write** (Studio › Access › org-wide defaults, or a metadata save) and publishes. A member whose permission set grants Read + Edit on that object can now **read** another user's record, but **editing** it is refused with the record-level sentence *"You do not have access to this record…"*.

The same object declared `public_read_write` from its **first** publish lets the same member edit (2xx). The only difference between the two objects is whether the OWD was changed after the first publish.

This contradicts the ruling #8023 landed in PR #8072: a `public_read_write` OWD opens row-level updates, not just the creator's.

- Fail-closed: this is over-refusal, and nothing is exposed.
- The step-by-step reproduction is withheld from this card, per the maintainer's instruction for authorization defects. It goes to the implementer privately.

## Measured

- Repo `3fcafcd3`, rerun on `origin/main` `898703f9`. No commit to `plugin-security` or `plugin-sharing` lies in between.
- 2026-10-27: two independent reproductions on a fresh probe package, plus one control object declared `public_read_write` from birth (2xx). One reproduction used an object the member had never touched before the change.
- The Studio QA Access card reproduced it independently on its own server.

## Landing site (suspected — the implementer verifies)

- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts`: the per-object posture (`owdOpensRowWrites`, written by `owdDeclaresOpenRowWrites`) appears not to be re-derived when a published object's `sharingModel` changes.
- Reads (the sharing service) do pick the change up, so it is the security plugin's posture/collection path, not the OWD itself.
- The existing pin `packages/qa/dogfood/test/owd-public-read-write-write-floor.dogfood.test.ts` only boots objects with their final OWD, so it cannot see a change at runtime.

## Acceptance

- After an OWD change to `public_read_write` is published (no restart), a member with Edit on the object can update a row they did not create.
- The reverse change (`public_read_write` → `private` / `public_read`) brings the creator-only update floor back.
- The delete floor is unchanged. #7792's by-id write-visibility property still holds.
- A pin that changes the OWD at runtime and asserts both directions over HTTP.

## Filing facts

- Business reason: admins tighten or open an object's OWD as their data model matures, and Studio's OWD panel exists for that. Today opening it silently fails for members until the next restart (suspected), so "everyone edits" does not work for the teams that turn it on.
- Reader who acts: an `os-dev` implementer, dispatched directly by this PM session on the maintainer's instruction (`domain:server`).
- Dedupe: semantic search `public_read_write sharing model changed after publish member update still refused owner_only_writes floor` on objectstack-ai/objectstack → 30 hits. No open duplicate; the nearest is closed #8023 (the origin ruling), and closed #25549 is a different path (external members).
- Source: Studio QA run, 2026-10-27, coordinator session `session_01J8VVAkZns5rNnK2rtszzbQ`.
